intended_object: The adjacency relation of the diameter graph of a planar point set: two distinct points are adjacent when their distance equals the diameter. Here the squared diameter is passed in as the parameter `D`. This comes from the docstring and from the module's Hopf–Pannwitz development.
explanation:
`Point` is `ℝ × ℝ` and `sqDist` is the squared Euclidean distance. `DiameterAdj D p q` says `p ≠ q ∧ sqDist p q = D`. When `D` is the squared diameter of `X` (`IsSqDiameter X D`), this says exactly that `p` and `q` are distinct points at the diameter distance, which is the edge relation of the diameter graph.

The relation is stated on all of the plane, not just on `X`. The library applies it to points of `X`, so this does not change anything. The condition `p ≠ q` is redundant when `D > 0`, but it keeps the relation irreflexive in every case, as a graph adjacency should be.

On generality: the module is a planar development of the Hopf–Pannwitz theorem, which is specifically a result about the plane. The whole project works in `ℝ × ℝ` with explicit coordinates, cross products and dot products. Mathlib has no "diameter graph" notion that this definition duplicates, so it is not `too_narrow`. The definition is a faithful, if simple, encoding of the intended relation.
